appraisal_events.evidence: "C'est autre chose, que vous connaissez probablement mieux que moi, ce sont de jeunes bourgeois" ... "peut-être aussi pour ne pas résister au plaisir de me témoigner quelque insolence"
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus delivers a class-tinged dig distinguishing his own milieu from the narrator's, and the text explicitly states he may be indulging the pleasure of showing the narrator some insolence; the narrator's own lack of amour-propre absorbs it without visible offense.

appraisal_events.evidence: "Est-ce que M. Ski n'est pas comme cela ?" ... "Mais pas du tout ... il a du charme et je lui trouve même quelque chose de très attachant."
appraisal_events.explanation: Brichot floats an insinuation about M. Ski's reputation, which Charlus sharply rejects before closing with a genuine compliment on his charm, a net positive but initially fraught local movement.

appraisal_events.evidence: "la situation de Mme de Villeparisis ... n'avait pas paru moins grande tout à fait à l'autre extrémité du monde ... aux Guermantes. Or celui-ci était plus brillant pour Mme de Villeparisis que je n'avais cru."
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus's revelations about her lineage (niece of a celebrated duchess) lead the narrator to conclude that Mme de Villeparisis holds more real prestige within the true aristocracy than her apparent social exclusion had suggested.

status_effects.explanation: Charlus's pointed class remark mildly positions the narrator as outside his own aristocratic frame, though the jab lands without visible effect on the narrator.
After Brichot's insinuation, Charlus's firm denial and praise leave M. Ski's local standing slightly improved.
Revelation of her aristocratic lineage and standing among the Guermantes elevates her local social position beyond what the narrator had previously assumed.
